name: ML-2
type: linear turn policy over finger movement only, trained on the game simulation
recognizer: LearnedRecognizer (app/src/main/java/com/davidsnake/game/Recognizers.kt); Python twin: tools/simlearn.py Policy + features
input: the current stroke's finger samples (time ms; x, y in dp rounded to 0.1 dp, as logged) and David's heading (a queued turn counts)
decides: once per game tick, just before it (the engine acts on a turn at the next tick), on the stroke's latest sample, if samples arrived since its last decision; a lifted or replaced stroke's last samples are decided at the next tick, and then a new stroke's samples wait one more tick
window_travel: from the first sample at or after (t - window) to the latest sample t
features: fwd40: finger travel along David's heading over the last 40 ms, per 20 dp
side40: finger travel to David's right over the last 40 ms, per 20 dp
fwd80: finger travel along David's heading over the last 80 ms, per 20 dp
side80: finger travel to David's right over the last 80 ms, per 20 dp
fwd160: finger travel along David's heading over the last 160 ms, per 20 dp
side160: finger travel to David's right over the last 160 ms, per 20 dp
fwd300: finger travel along David's heading over the last 300 ms, per 20 dp
side300: finger travel to David's right over the last 300 ms, per 20 dp
speed: finger travel over the last 40 ms, per 500 dp/s
since: ms since the last-turn sample, at most 400, per 400
fwdSince: finger travel along the heading since the last-turn sample, per 40 dp
sideSince: finger travel to David's right since the last-turn sample, per 40 dp
scores: none = 0; right = w_side . f; left = w_side . mirror(f), mirror negating the side features; back = w_back . sym(f), sym zeroing them; the highest wins, ties going to the first of none, right, left, back

commands.back: with a tail, a U-turn: first to the side the finger's travel over the last 160 ms leans to by 3 dp or more, else the side with more free cells ahead (never a blocked side if the other is open), then back, which the engine holds until the first turn's step; without a tail, a reversal

last_turn: after a decision's commands run, if David's heading changed, the latest sample becomes the last-turn sample; it starts at the stroke's first sample

training.deterministic: re-running the command on the same files gives identical weights
training.method: learning to search on the window simulation (tools/windowsim.py): in every gesture window of the training games the model plays the window; at each tick it decided, each of the four answers is tried, the model deciding the rest; the four window scores are that tick's example; weights minimize the expected loss against the best answer (softmax, L2) by Adam; examples accumulate over rounds; round 0 copies the live game's own turns

objective.windows: one per gesture start: finger speed rising from under 60 to over 150 dp/s with 10 dp of travel, or a turn of 60 degrees or more while moving (speed over 40 ms)
objective.run: after the input David goes straight until he eats the harp or dies
objective.harp: +1 for eating the harp, whenever it happens (only the first); the run ends there
objective.death: -0.5 times exp(-(s - 1) / decay), s = steps from the window start to the death, decay by cause; a spear hitting David from the side (flying across the direction of his last step) costs nothing
objective.spears: recorded throws aimed before the window started (throw tick <= start + 18)

training.result: 3-fold cross-validation by game (game i of the files in order is in fold i % 3), per 1000 gestures on validation games: ML-2 436.0, ML-1 438.7, S2-FAST 429.8; ML-2 minus S2-FAST +6.2 (90% range -0.3 to +13.0); this model is then trained on all the games
